$comment: Regression ceilings for `check-thresholds`, in nanoseconds, compared against
criterion's median point estimate for each benchmark id.
These are ORDER-OF-MAGNITUDE DETECTORS, NOT SLOs. Each ceiling is 10x the
median measured on the reference machine documented in benches/README.md.
That headroom exists because this gate runs on shared CI runners, which are
several times slower than a developer machine and vary run to run. The
practical effect is that a regression of roughly 3x or more on CI hardware
fails the build, while ordinary drift does not.
The measured tables in benches/README.md are the real baseline for judging
a change. Raise a ceiling only alongside a deliberate, explained change in
what the runtime does — never to turn a red build green.
The gRPC arms are deliberately absent: they cross loopback TCP, which is the
least reproducible thing in the suite on a shared runner. They are published
as a comparison baseline, not gated.
